mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, treat both sides as signed equations preserving the order of the names as they appear.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence has the form 'The number of X that A has more/fewer than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C and D have' (or any similar equality of differences).
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'The number of oranges that Alice has more than Bob is equal to the difference between the number of oranges that Carol and Dave have' as |Alice - Bob| = |Carol - Dave| (absolute values) instead of preserving sign.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known (through a direct count, a solved equation, or a transfer), substitute that value into all other equations and constraints, and propagate any newly determined values repeatedly until no further deductions are possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each statement that fixes a variable's count, update all pending equations that involve that variable.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a newly known value into other equations, leaving them unsolved.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the text, after applying all earlier statements (including transfers and direct counts).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a 'has K more/fewer than' or a difference equality that appears after some transfers or overrides.
mathgap.example: Treating a comparative statement as if it referred to the initial counts, ignoring earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations and variables that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before attempting to solve the whole system, especially when many statements are irrelevant to the query.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system, including many unrelated variables, leading to unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similarly spelled names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a problem contains many similar‑sounding or similar‑looking names.
mathgap.example: Merging 'Alphonse' and 'Alphonse' incorrectly, or confusing 'Ada' with 'Adam'.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says 'the difference between the number of X that A and B have', interpret it as A - B, preserving the order as written, rather than taking the absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement contains the phrase 'difference between ... A and B'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between the number of apples that Alice and Bob have' as |Alice - Bob| instead of Alice - Bob.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as A - B = K, and 'A has K fewer than B' as A - B = -K, preserving the sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any comparative statement using 'more' or 'fewer'.
mathgap.example: Swapping the direction and writing B - A = K for 'A has K more than B'.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N items', set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears, regardless of earlier statements about that person.
mathgap.example: Treating a later 'X has N' as an initial count and ignoring earlier transfers that changed X's count.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver, using the current counts at that point.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'X gives K to Y' statement appears.
mathgap.example: Applying transfers out of order, causing counts to be incorrect.

mathgap.title: Nested Difference Phrase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses a nested phrase like 'the number of X that A has more than B' (or 'has fewer than B'), interpret it as the signed difference A - B, not as an absolute value or a separate count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a difference phrase appears as a noun phrase within a larger statement, such as 'The number of oranges that Alice has more than Bob is 5'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the number of oranges that Alice has more than Bob' as a separate variable instead of the signed difference Alice - Bob.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often interprets 'A has K more than B' as B - A = K, reversing the intended sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map 'A has K more than B' to A - B = K; for 'fewer' use A - B = -K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes 'difference' means magnitude, ignoring sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve order and sign when interpreting 'difference between A and B' as A - B.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers as if they were simultaneous or in arbitrary order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfers sequentially in the order they appear in the text.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are always initial, not overrides.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears later, overwrite the current value for that person.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model sometimes reads 'twice as many' or similar as addition rather than multiplication.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize multiplicative language and apply appropriate arithmetic.
